cornerCallouts: Here they go through Hatzenbach, a fast and flowing complex that requires absolute precision. Any mistake here can have serious consequences.
Into Flugplatz now, where the cars can get some serious air! It's crucial to keep it smooth through this section to avoid damage.
They're approaching Schwedenkreuz, one of the fastest and most challenging corners on the Nordschleife. Brave doesn't even begin to describe it.
Through Aremberg now, a deceptively tricky corner that has caught out many drivers over the years. It's all about maintaining momentum.
Hohe Acht is next, a blind crest that leads into a downhill section. It's a real test of commitment and car control.
They're now navigating the Karussell, the legendary banked corner. It's brutal on the suspension but provides incredible grip.
Now the drivers face Brünnchen, a popular spectating spot and another section where overtaking is possible. The crowd is going wild!
Into the final sector, where the cars blast through the pit straight and over the start/finish line. It's going to be a nail-biting finish.
strategyPoints: Tire management will be crucial over this 25.378km lap, especially in the high-speed sections of the Nordschleife. Expect to see varied strategies throughout the race.
Fuel consumption is always a factor here, but the sheer length of the lap means teams need to balance pace with fuel efficiency. The pit window will be a key consideration.
With such a long lap, the timing of safety cars will be critical. A well-timed pit stop under safety car conditions can gain a team valuable track position.
The Nordschleife is notoriously unforgiving, and mechanical failures are common. Reliability will be just as important as outright speed.
The weather can change in an instant at the Nürburgring. Teams need to be prepared to switch to wet tires at a moment's notice.
Traffic management is key on this long and twisty circuit. Overtaking can be difficult, so drivers need to be patient and pick their moments carefully.
The 24h Combined layout puts immense strain on the brakes. Teams will need to monitor brake wear closely throughout the race.
Communication between the driver and the team is vital. With such a challenging circuit, drivers need to be able to provide accurate feedback on the car's performance.
weatherCommentary: The Eifel mountains are known for their unpredictable weather. Rain clouds are gathering on the horizon, and a downpour could be just around the corner.
The fog can roll in quickly at the Nürburgring, especially around the Nordschleife. Visibility can be reduced to almost zero in some sections.
The wind is picking up, which can make the cars feel unstable in the high-speed corners. Drivers will need to adjust their driving style accordingly.
The sun is shining brightly today, but the temperature is still relatively cool. Tire warm-up could be a challenge in the early stages of the race.
There's a chance of thunderstorms later in the day. The teams will be keeping a close eye on the radar.
